q-122214.name: Question 1
q-122214.worked_solution:
The formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r}$ is given by

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\,.
$$

Substituting $n=20$ and $r=5$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{20}{P}_{5} & =\frac{20!}{(20-5)!} \\  & =\frac{20!}{15!} \\  & =\frac{20\cdot 19\cdot 18\cdot 17\cdot 16\cdot \cancel{15!}}{\cancel{15!}} \\  & =20\cdot 19\cdot 18\cdot 17\cdot 16 \\  & =1\,860\,480.\end{aligned}
$$

q-122230.name: Question 5
q-122230.problem: A cook designs a menu for his restaurant from Thursday to Sunday. Each day, only one main dish will be served, and it will not be repeated on any other day. If the cook wants to choose from the $9$ most popular dishes, how many different menus can the cook design?
q-122230.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $9$ popular dishes to choose from, so $n=9.$ We want to select $4$ of those for the menu, one for each day (Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday), so we have $r=4.$ 

Therefore, the number of different choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{P}_{4} & =\frac{9!}{(9-4)!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{5!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}} \\  & =9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6 \\  & =3\,024.\end{aligned}
$$

q-84982.name: Question 6
q-84982.problem: Victoria has the $4$ playing cards: the ace of clubs, the ace of diamonds, the ace of hearts, and the ace of spades. She takes one card and places it in front of her. She then does the same with another card. In how many different ways can she choose a sequence of $2$ cards like this?
q-84982.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $4$ cards, so $n=4.$ We want to select $2$ of those cards to make a sequence of $2$ cards, so we have $r=2.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to choose the cards is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{4}{P}_{2} & =\frac{4!}{(4-2)!} \\  & =\frac{4!}{2!} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{\cancel{2!}} \\  & =4\cdot 3 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

q-84984.problem: A soccer coach must choose a defensive lineup for each of the $4$ defensive positions from a roster of $11$ defenders. How many potential starting defensive lineups are there?

q-5558.name: Question 8
q-5558.problem: How many different arrangements of gold, silver, and bronze medalists can there be out of $10$ Olympic athletes, assuming there are no ties?
q-5558.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $10$ athletes, so $n=10.$ We want to select $3$ of those athletes to receive gold, silver, or bronze medals, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different ways to award the medals is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{10}{P}_{3} & =\frac{10!}{(10-3)!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{7!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot \cancel{7!}}{\cancel{7!}} \\  & =10\cdot 9\cdot 8 \\  & =720.\end{aligned}
$$
